subject: Request: hosted API per-1M token pricing and supported model roster
messages:
From: Alison Park <alison.park@syncwise.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hosted API per-1M token pricing and supported model roster

Hi Lukas,

We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot (SyncWise) and I need your standard hosted API 'per 1M token' rates broken out by input vs output. Specifically:

- Baseline per-1M token rates (input vs output) across your recommended hosted models (small / mid / large).
- A roster of supported models for generation/chat and embeddings (which models are eligible for hosted API).
- Any standard volume/commit discount tiers and what triggers them (1M, 10M, 50M+ tokens).
- Whether you offer short-term pilot pricing or one-off promotional discounts for proofs-of-concept.

To give context: our expected pilot profile is ~10M tokens/month, ~70% generation/chat (1.5–2k output per request on average), ~30% embedding calls (short input). Procurement also needs the SOW line items and any SOC 2 statements you can share.

Can you send a concise ratecard and the model roster (or a link) today? We're trying to lock down a vendor for a July POC. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Alison Park
Director of Product, SyncWise
alison.park@syncwise.com
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@syncwise.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API per-1M token pricing and supported model roster

Hi Alison — thanks for the detail and the timeline. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Marissa (solutions) to put together a concise ratecard + model roster and SOC2 artifacts. A couple of quick clarifying Qs that will help us give the tightest estimate:

1) For embeddings you mention "short input" — do you mean you expect <128 tokens per embedding call or closer to 256–512? That changes the effective per-1M cost for embeddings.
2) For generation, is the 1.5–2k output per request inclusive of the prompt tokens (i.e., total IO) or is that strictly output tokens?

Ben/Marissa — can you please prepare:
- Per-1M token input / output baseline rates by model family (small / mid / flagship)
- A short example cost table (we'll show the math for an expected 10M token month with the IO split Alison provided)
- Any pilot discount options and the standard trigger points for volume discounts
- Attach SOC2 evidence and SOW line items for procurement

Will follow up once they send the materials.

Cheers,
Lukas Meyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@syncwise.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API per-1M token pricing and supported model roster

Hi Alison — thanks for the note and context. Attaching a concise ratecard and the model roster; below is the baseline hosted pricing and a worked example for the 10M token/month pilot you described. Attachments: Redwood-hosted-ratecard-2026.pdf, model-compatibility-roster-2026.csv (stubs included).

Baseline hosted IO rates (per 1M tokens):
- Small (s-7b family) 
  - Input: $0.30 per 1M tokens
  - Output: $1.00 per 1M tokens
- Mid (m-13b family)
  - Input: $0.80 per 1M tokens
  - Output: $2.40 per 1M tokens
- Flagship (r-70b class)
  - Input: $1.50 per 1M tokens
  - Output: $5.20 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings (emb-2.x family)
  - Per 1M tokens (short inputs typical): $4.00 per 1M tokens

Notes: these are hosted API list rates for IO billing. Embeddings are billed on tokenized input length; if your average embedding input is <128 tokens we can show the adjusted math (see example).

Example cost for expected pilot (10M total tokens/month, split 70% generation/chat, 30% embeddings):
- Assumptions: generation uses Mid family (m-13b), embeddings use emb-2.x with avg 100 tokens per call.
- Generation IO (70% of 10M = 7M tokens): assume of those 7M, 30% are input and 70% are output (roughly 2.1M input / 4.9M output).
  - Gen input cost: 2.1 * $0.80 = $1.68 (per 1M tokens -> scaled to 2.1M = $1.68)
  - Gen output cost: 4.9 * $2.40 = $11.76
- Embeddings (30% of 10M = 3M tokens) at $4.00 per 1M = $12.00
- Total monthly (list rates): ~$25.44 for 10M tokens under these assumptions (example purpose — we'll provide a spreadsheet with row-level math).

Volume/commit discount guidance (standard):
- 0–5M tokens/month: list rates apply
- 5M–50M tokens/month: 10% discount available with a 3-month minimum commitment
- 50M–250M tokens/month: 18% discount with a 6-month minimum commit
- 250M+ tokens/month: custom pricing (negotiated)

Pilot discounts / one-offs:
- We can offer a one-time pilot discount up to 20% for a 3-month POC, capped at a defined usage amount (we typically set a monthly cap; see attached sample SOW).

Procurement artifacts provided: SOC 2 Type II summary, SOW template, and a short procurement checklist (attached). For your procurement team, the SOW line item we recommend is: Hosted API consumption (per-token IO billing), plus optional Dedicated reservation if you need guaranteed throughput.

HubSpot link to this opportunity: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/9876543 (shared for your procurement).

If you'd like, we can convert this into a short one-page proposal / quote with a 3-month pilot discount and PO instructions.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that breakdown is really helpful and the worked example clarifies a lot. A few next items from our side: 

- Would you be able to produce a 3-month pilot quote with the 20% pilot discount you mentioned? We'd propose a capped monthly usage of 12M tokens for the pilot. Please include a simple PO flow so procurement can approve quickly.
- We will need the SOC 2 evidence (summary is fine) and the SOW line item phrased for our legal/procurement; thanks for the attachments — can you confirm the SOW includes a 30-day termination clause?
- Also: if we choose the Mid family for generation but want to failover to Small (s-7b) during traffic spikes, is smart routing and fallback covered under the hosted plan or is that part of a Dedicated offering?

If you can send a short pilot quote and updated SOW this afternoon that would be ideal — otherwise we can take the docs and propose internally tomorrow.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alison
